images.title: Holes: old ones stay, new ones join
images.purpose: Show that the holes at a step are the old holes plus one new hole for every square of the step before.
images.composition: One large Step 2 Sierpinski Carpet centred on white, with the old hole in one colour and the new holes in another, and one short sum underneath.
images.exact_structure: One large square, about 60 percent of the frame height, centred, drawn as a 9 by 9 grid of equal small squares. Remaining squares are filled teal #0072B2 with thin dark outlines. The central 3 by 3 block (rows 4 to 6, columns 4 to 6) is one big white hole outlined in grey #6B7280: this is the 1 old hole. In each of the 8 outer 3 by 3 blocks, its centre small square is a white hole outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7: these are the 8 new holes, exactly 8. Remaining small squares: 81 minus 9 minus 8 = 64, all teal. Label 'old hole' with a thin grey pointer to the big hole, '8 new holes' with a thin purple pointer to one small hole. Under the carpet, centred, the sum '1 + 8 = 9 holes', and below it in smaller type 'Step 3: 9 + 64 = 73'. Above the carpet, 'Step 2'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Old holes stay, and every square of the step before adds one new hole.

image_decisions.why: The rule H(n + 1) = Hn + Rn is seen by telling old holes from new holes in one picture.
